failures.summary: No-early-stop replay does not reproduce the renderer's early-stop semantics; 61/64 deletion comparisons passed, max relative error 0.51527848, replay max abs 0.00954908.
failures.resolution: Exact CUDA counterfactual replay now matches renderer early-stop semantics, including removal of the stopping gate. Validation passes 64/64, replay max abs is 0, and max relative error is 2.40445e-6. Formal K2 cache d5073d9d688b15063013e59bf67524819aa99f033b67c6e3f2d0967542788014 completed.

failures.summary: OpenCV H.264 decoding corrupted R1 and one R2 evaluation pass. Built a derived frame cache accepted only when reference PSNR matched the frozen P00 per-frame value within 1e-5, then reran R1/R2. Original outputs remain under runs/research/P01/decode_invalid/.
Only 13/63862 dynamic points pass the frozen opacity and 2-degree rotation gates. Reachable saving is 13000 bytes versus a 31931000-byte target; the gates were not relaxed.
The 128-trajectory algorithm smoke completed, but writing its result failed because the P15 output root did not yet exist. The output root is now created before the smoke; no formal run had started.

The segment proxy is anti-correlated with the negative true development-view segment error (Spearman -0.542857). Five MW rounds are numerically indistinguishable from one uniform round and do not improve P02/P03/P01.

Four-round fresh K2 recalibration changes boundary IDs after millions of newly exposed contributor rays, but lowers PSNR by 0.385796 dB and worsens worst-10% drop by 0.823569 dB versus the stale/P02 control. All correctness checks pass.
K3 ordered per-ray alpha/color lists and exact joint replay are unavailable; K1/K2 aggregates cannot substitute without changing the registered method.
K3 signed per-ray RGB deletion vectors are unavailable; squared K2 e_it cannot recover signs and is explicitly disallowed as a substitute.

All 256 highest-risk feasible reappearance demands are already satisfied by the P02 set, so the registered monotone repair makes zero swaps. R0 and R1 are exactly identical globally, temporally, and in reappearance patches.

Across seeds 0/1/2, hard-STE R0 and soft-then-hard R1 trail equal-step ordinary-finetuning R2 by 2.640835 dB and 1.878369 dB. R1's dense soft state averages 31.940622 dB but loses 6.068814 dB on exact-budget hardening. R2 improves +0.499756 dB over P02 zero-FT, attributing the positive gain to extra training rather than learned selection.

Global top-K reallocates 1,176 points from static to dynamic, costs +1,176,000 bytes, and changes PSNR by -0.001150 dB. Risk balancing reallocates 5,403 points, costs +5,403,000 bytes, and lowers PSNR by 0.072804 dB. Neither count- nor byte-aware evidence supports the reallocation.

Moment-matched merging loses 4.504748 dB PSNR and worsens LPIPS by 0.190864 versus the exact same-ID, same-byte keep-parent control. Static merging has ample opportunity (46,767 retained merges), while only 430 dynamic merged parents survive the frozen trajectory and opacity gates.

The switching penalty cuts proxy switches by 52.95% and teacher-residual TDE by 18.20%, but registered GT-residual TDE improves only 0.2289% versus gamma=0. End-to-end gather plus render is 30.65-32.25% slower than the full-model baseline, and both rules have a dynamic-group budget gap.

At the same byte cap, E/byte improves PSNR by 0.194087 dB and LPIPS by 0.003137 over the pure-E packing control. At exactly the same 50% tile cap, E/tile improves PSNR by 1.342975 dB and LPIPS by 0.010470, while measured wall latency is 7.51% lower than the matched control and 48.24% lower than the full-model baseline. Byte and tile tracks remain separate trade-offs.

The required K3 ordered per-ray direction/weight/color cache does not exist. K1 aggregates and squared K2 deletion errors cannot recover the registered per-option SH distortion D_io, so no substitute or formal run was made.

seed_policy.deterministic_methods: verify seed-invariant IDs and evaluate once; do not report duplicate runs as independent samples
